body:
# Independent audit: sampled folding fails even the continuous Gamma_3 bound


`candidate 59fbb688156c4bcd`.

Result: **PASS**, with the source's stated restriction that the folding
anchor is an interior point but is not a deepest mixed-integer point.
No correction to the certificate or to its scope is needed.

## Actual fibers and exact pushforward measure

For `T=conv{(0,0),(1,0),(0,1)}`, let `V=|T|=1/2`. The body

    C=conv({-1}x(7T/15), {0}xT, {1}xT)

is compact, convex, full-dimensional, and has exactly three integer
bases. Its endpoint sections are the displayed triangles. Its section
at zero is the convex hull of T and `(7T/15+T)/2=11T/15`, hence is
exactly T. Therefore its total mixed area is

    (49/225+1+1)V=(499/225)V.

The two largest fibers have area V, strictly smaller than half this
total since `499/450>1`. No fiber is omitted from this calculation.

The point `p=(1/300,1/300)` is strictly inside T. Under the specified
map `(z,x) -> (x-zp)/(1-z)`, the selected fiber at zero is unchanged,
while the fiber at -1 is mapped by `x -> (x+p)/2`. The latter map has
area Jacobian 1/4. Its image is

    (7/30)T + (1/600,1/600).

Its density is consequently 4, and adding the unchanged fiber gives
exactly the source density, including overlaps. The folded total is

    (1+4(7/30)^2)V=(274/225)V.

This is a pushforward of the two selected fiber measures. It is not
an assertion that the map preserves the mixed-integer lattice, and the
source does not use it that way.

## Plane cover and cap areas

Use `s=27/50`, `r=4/15`, and `k=99/500`. The identity

    2k=(1-r)s

is exact. If a point lies outside both closed halfspaces
`x-r y>=k` and `y-r x>=k`, adding the two strict failures gives
`(1-r)(x+y)<(1-r)s`. Since `1-r>0`, the point belongs to the remaining
halfspace `x+y<=s`. The three closed halfspaces therefore cover the
whole plane, including all boundaries. Every point belongs to a cap
whose folded mass is at most the largest of these three masses. This
proves the required upper bound on maximal continuous depth without
any assumption about an attained optimizer or its location.

The `x+y<=s` trace on T is the triangle sT, of relative area s^2.
The smaller translated triangle is wholly inside this cap because

    7/30+2/600=71/300 < 27/50.

Its full relative weighted area is `4(7/30)^2`. Thus the first cap's
mass divided by V is exactly `11461/22500`.

For the second cap, a triangle of scale a at the origin cut by
`x-r y>=h`, where `0<h<a`, has relative area

    (a-h)^2/(1+r)

when divided by V. This follows from its three vertices on `y=0`
and `x+y=a`; its horizontal base length is `a-h` and its altitude is
`(a-h)/(1+r)`. Applying this first with `a=1,h=k`, and then to the
small triangle after translating its origin, gives the source formula.
The translated threshold is

    k'=k-(1-r)/600=1771/9000,
    0 < k' < 7/30=2100/9000.

All the uses of the triangle formula are therefore in its stated
nondegenerate range. Substitution gives

    b1=[(1-k)^2+4(7/30-k')^2]/(1+r)
       =6566561/12825000.

Coordinate symmetry proves the same formula for the third cap. Exact
subtraction, performed independently with rational arithmetic, gives

    b1-b0=33791/12825000>0.

The maximal normalized depth is consequently at most

    b1/(274/225)=6566561/15618000.

The difference from Gamma_3 is exactly

    27/64-6566561/15618000=89131/62472000>0.

These are exact polygon-area calculations. No numerical optimizer,
empirical claim about directions, or unverified limiting argument is
used. The finite union of line boundaries has zero area for each of
the two absolutely continuous density components.

## Erosion is present; deepest-contact status is absent

The relevant perspective sections can be written explicitly as

    B_t=(1-t)C_(-t/(1-t))+t p.

For `0<=s<t<1` with the remote section present, actual convexity gives

    B_t+(t-s)(T-p) subset B_s.

Indeed the left side equals
`(1-t)C_(-t/(1-t))+(t-s)T+s p`, which is contained in
`(1-s)C_(-s/(1-s))+s p` by the exact affine relation between the
three base coordinates. Since p is in the interior of T, `T-p`
contains zero in its interior and any transverse central section
has positive length. Thus the ordinary erosion information claimed
in the source is genuinely available in this actual body.

The anchor is nonetheless far from deepest. The own-fiber cap
`x+y<=1/150` passes through p and has area `V/22500`. It is isolated
from both other integer fibers by the actual ambient halfspace

    -x-y+(z-1)>=-1/150.

On the fiber at 1 this is exactly the own cap. At bases 0 and -1,
all fiber coordinates are nonnegative and the inequality fails
strictly. Thus the anchor has raw mixed depth at most `V/22500`.
At the centroid of the middle T, ordinary planar Grünbaum applied
to the own-fiber trace of every nonvertical containing halfspace
gives raw mixed depth at least `(4/9)V`; pure-integer containing
halfspaces include the whole own fiber. The anchor is therefore not
a globally deepest contact.

The source correctly keeps this certificate separate from the
genuine-two-contact example that only disproves Ball-body convexity.
This certificate rules out a continuous Gamma_3 depth conclusion from
actual convex compatibility, erosion, an interior neighboring anchor,
and the no-heavy-fiber condition alone. It does not rule out an
additional theorem requiring genuine deepest contacts, and it is not
an OC counterexample.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
